archetype.name: Rebuilding (offense ahead of defense)
archetype.definition: A team in its third straight losing season whose young-QB offense has climbed to roughly league average while a defense that was a top-10 unit last year has fallen apart, leaving a 2-5 record that is about what its play deserves.

report.headline: Shough's offense is respectable now; the defense that carried 2025 has collapsed.
report.take:
The Saints are a team whose two halves have traded places. In 2025 the offense ranked 27th in EPA and scored 18 points a game, and a 10th-ranked defense kept them in games. Seven weeks into 2026, Tyler Shough has started every game and the scoring offense is middle of the pack at 23.1 points a game (17th). The defense now ranks 26th in EPA allowed and 28th in points allowed. A net EPA ranked 27th is a bad-team number, and the record matches it. They are 2-5 with one win fewer than the point differential implies. That is a little unlucky, not a hidden contender.

The defense is the story, and it starts on the ground. They are dead last in rush EPA allowed and 31st in success rate allowed, so opponents stay on schedule. That shows up on third down, where they rank 29th. Atlanta ran for 205 yards in a 45-24 rout, and three other opponents cleared 140. The pass rush makes sacks (18, 10th) without making much pressure (27th in pressure rate). When coverage breaks, it breaks deep: they rank 31st in EPA allowed on deep throws. The NFC South is weak enough that none of this is fatal yet, since the division leader is 3-5. But this is not a defense that can protect a lead.

The offense is real in one way and hollow in another. The line pass-protects well (12th in pressure rate allowed, 13th in sack rate), and Shough has had big days: +10.9 passing EPA at Baltimore and +10.6 against Pittsburgh. He has also had a -11.9 day against Minnesota. The run game has done almost nothing. They average 3.13 yards a carry (30th) with a 31st-ranked run success rate, and they managed 18 rushing yards against the Steelers. The backfield has rotated among Kendre Miller, Alvin Kamara and an injured Travis Etienne. Thirteen turnovers have handed back much of what the passing game builds. Three games of three or more giveaways explain most of the losses better than the defense does.

Where this goes depends on two things. One is whether the turnovers settle down, which tends to happen. The other is whether the run defense can get even to below average, which is harder because it comes from a broken front, not bad luck. Kellen Moore's aggression helps: every fourth-down chance taken, and 7th in short-yardage conversion. Expect a team that plays more competitive games than its record suggests and still loses more than it wins.

strengths.title: Scoring offense back to league average
strengths.body: After two years near the bottom, the offense is scoring 23.1 points a game, 17th in the league, under a single starter at quarterback. The passing game has a real ceiling when Shough keeps the ball safe: two games with double-digit passing EPA. It is built on Chris Olave's target volume more than on efficiency, so it is a floor more than a weapon.

strengths.title: Pass protection holds up
strengths.body: The line ranks 12th in pressure rate allowed and 13th in sack rate even though Shough holds the ball fairly long (27th in time to throw). That gives the passing game a stable base and lets Moore stay pass-heavy. This should last, though guard Cesar Ruiz's knee is the risk to watch.

strengths.title: Aggressive, effective in short yardage
strengths.body: Moore has gone for it on every fourth-down chance the model flags, the most aggressive rate in the league. The offense converts short yardage at the 7th-best rate. For an underdog-quality roster, extra possessions and drives kept alive add up over a season.

concerns.title: Run defense is the league's worst
concerns.body: The Saints are last in rush EPA allowed and 31st in success rate allowed, so opponents stay ahead of the chains and convert third downs at the 29th-worst rate. This is a sharp break from a defense that ranked 10th last year, which points to a front problem rather than a fluke. It is the weakness most likely to persist. Deep coverage (31st in deep EPA allowed) is a second leak behind it.

concerns.title: Turnovers erase the passing gains
concerns.body: Thirteen giveaways in seven games, with three or more in each of the losses to Detroit, Las Vegas and Minnesota, put the turnover margin at 26th. Turnover rates tend to come down, so this is the most likely thing to improve. A young quarterback leaning on volume throwing keeps the risk elevated.

concerns.title: No functioning run game
concerns.body: At 3.13 yards a carry with a 31st-ranked run success rate, the ground game gives Shough no help on early downs. The line is 26th in yards before contact, so the problem starts up front, not only with the rotating backs. The 18-yard game against Pittsburgh shows how one-dimensional it can get against a good front.

trend.note: The season has swung from a near-upset in Detroit and a win in Baltimore to three straight losses. A 4-takeaway win over the Giants followed, then a 10-16 loss to Pittsburgh. Passing EPA has swung from strongly negative to strongly positive with no steady pattern.

nextGame.headline: Off a bye, Saints face a Browns team winning above its play
nextGame.body:
Cleveland's 5-3 record is built on close games. The Browns are 2nd in wins over expected and win 83% of one-score games, but they carry a negative point differential and rank 17th in net EPA. Their offense is 24th in EPA and can't run the ball (27th in rush EPA). Watson takes sacks at the league's worst rate, behind a line that also draws penalties constantly. Their defense is the real unit, 7th against the pass by EPA. The flaw is on the ground: the Browns allow the most explosive runs in the league and miss tackles at the worst rate. The Book has New Orleans as a 2.5-point home favorite indoors with a 43.5 total. The Saints are coming off 14 days of rest after the Paris game.

Availability leans on the Saints' side of the report. Safety Justin Reid (93% of snaps) is questionable after his concussion in Paris. That matters for a defense already leaking deep. Guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DT Nathan Shepherd (illness) are also questionable, and the loss of either thins a weak run front or a solid pass-protection unit. Etienne is on IR, leaving Kendre Miller and Alvin Kamara at running back. A decision on opening rookie-type WR Jordyn Tyson's practice window is pending. Cleveland lists no injuries.

waysToWin.title: Feast on Cleveland's leaky protection
waysToWin.body: The Saints' defense finishes sacks well (11th in sack rate) even without much pressure. Cleveland allows sacks at the worst rate in the league and gets hit more than anyone. A few drive-killing sacks against an offense that already struggles to move the ball could keep this a low-scoring game the Saints control.

waysToWin.title: Pop runs through missed tackles
waysToWin.body: Cleveland is last in explosive run rate allowed and missed-tackle rate. A Saints run game that rarely gets clean yardage could still break one or two long ones. Even a couple of chunk runs would take pressure off Shough against a strong pass defense.

waysToWin.title: Win the penalty and hidden-yardage battle
waysToWin.body: Cleveland commits 9 penalties a game (31st), its line is flagged more than almost any other, and its special teams rank 22nd in EPA. New Orleans is disciplined by comparison. In a game projected around 43 points, free yards and drives extended by flags can decide it.

waysToLose.title: Giveaways hand Cleveland short fields
waysToLose.body: The Saints' losses have been defined by multi-turnover days, and Cleveland's offense can't score 20 on its own. Turning the ball over against a top-10 defense is the clearest way to let a weak offense steal a close one. Close games are where the Browns have thrived.

waysToLose.title: Shough stalls against a top pass defense
waysToLose.body: Cleveland ranks 7th in pass EPA allowed and shuts down tight ends (2nd in EPA per play to TE1), which takes away Juwan Johnson. With no running game to lean on, the Saints could look like they did against Minnesota's top defense. Their 13 points that day came with -11.9 passing EPA.

waysToLose.title: Run defense lets a bad ground game live
waysToLose.body: Cleveland can't run well, but the Saints have the league's worst rush defense by EPA. If the Browns stay on schedule on the ground, the third-down issues follow. That shortens a game the Saints need to be long, and it lets Watson avoid the obvious passing downs where he gets sacked.

nextGame.watch: Saints pass rush against Cleveland's protection on third down: if the Saints get Watson into obvious passing downs, their sack-finishing edge meets the league's worst sack-rate line.

restOfSeason.body:
The schedule has a mix of easier and tougher spots. Carolina twice and Arizona are winnable. Chicago, Cincinnati and Green Bay are a three-week gauntlet. Tampa Bay twice and Atlanta bring top-10 defenses. The offense's turnover rate should come down, which is the main source of improvement, and pass protection looks sturdy. The run defense is a structural problem and won't fix itself in-season. The run game is too, so the Saints will stay a pass-first team that has to play clean to win.

A weak division keeps the door technically open, since no NFC South team is above .500. But the underlying numbers describe a bottom-ten team, not a hidden contender. Realistically, this looks like another mid-single-digit win total. The season's value lies in Shough's development and finding answers on the defensive front for next year.
swingFactors: Health of Reid and the offensive line

confidence.note: Seven games, one quarterback, and a consistent efficiency picture, but turnovers and the defensive drop-off from 2025 can move fast.
